title: requests.get()
summary: Send an HTTP GET request. Always pass a timeout.
description: `requests` is not in the standard library, and it is not available in this sandbox — the lesson exercises use a stub client with the same shape. The API is worth knowing because it is what you will use in real work.

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Query parameters; correctly URL-encoded for you.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Seconds, or (connect, read). **Omitting it means wait for ever.**

examples.title: A correct call
examples.code:
r = requests.get(url, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {t}'},
                 timeout=10)
r.raise_for_status()
data = r.json()

examples.title: Reuse the connection
examples.code:
with requests.Session() as s:
    s.headers['Authorization'] = ...
    for page in range(10):
        s.get(url, params={'page': page},
                                          timeout=10)

real_world_usage: A Session reuses the TCP/TLS connection, which is often a 3–5× speedup over repeated `requests.get` for paginated APIs.

common_mistakes.fix: The default is to wait for ever. One hung server takes a worker with it.
A 404 body is still a body. Call raise_for_status() or check explicitly.

common_mistakes.mistake: verify=False to silence a TLS error
common_mistakes.fix: That disables certificate checking entirely. Fix the trust store.

performance_notes: Use a Session for connection pooling. Parallelise independent calls with a ThreadPoolExecutor (the work is I/O-bound, so the GIL is not a constraint) or use httpx with asyncio.
security_notes: Always HTTPS. Never log the Authorization header. Never fetch a user-supplied URL without an allowlist — that is server-side request forgery.
